answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a jury-duty liability mechanism, requiring each new identity to serve on a grading jury. As each additional identity is created, the inviter incurs escalating financial costs, as they must stake tokens that are slashed if their votes deviate from the consensus. For example, a single identity may cost 50 tokens, but with each new inlet, that cost could rise to 200 tokens, 500. The attacker ultimately faces substantial losses, similar to trying to hold back a tide with a single prism; every added identity weakens their position further.
